name: LLM Router for Orca
description: Use all your subscriptions and API credits from any provider and coding plan on any agent in Orca, in one place, without leaving Orca. Features multi-key credential pools with auto-rotation, load balancing, and routing different providers behind a single model name by prioritizing the fastest endpoint with seamless fallback.

settings.title: Route agent traffic
settings.description: When on, every enabled agent Orca launches is pointed at the sidecar. Turn individual agents off in the Agents tab.

settings.title: Also route Codex and OpenCode outside Orca
settings.description: Off by default, so only agents Orca launches are routed. When on, the router also adds its provider to ~/.codex/config.toml and the OpenCode user config so Orca's native Codex chat and a plain codex or opencode in any terminal use the gateway. That affects every Codex and OpenCode session on this machine while the router runs. Turning this off, stopping the router or disabling the plugin removes it again.

settings.title: Sidecar port
settings.description: Local port the gateway listens on. 18080 by default.

settings.title: Sidecar host
settings.description: Bind address. Keep 127.0.0.1 unless other machines must reach the gateway.

settings.title: Upstream timeout (ms)
settings.description: Per-request ceiling for one upstream attempt, including long streams. 600000 keeps 10-minute streams alive.

settings.title: Retries per upstream
settings.description: Retries after 429, 5xx and network errors before falling over to the next model in the chain.

settings.title: Retry backoff base (ms)
settings.description: Exponential backoff starts at this delay; a positive Retry-After wins.
